introduction: “The intention of the teacher must be pure, his heart independent, his spirit attracted.” These few passages are ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel to those who teach the Faith: seek no reward and no recognition, serve by conduct before words, know and respect the people one goes to, and attend first to one’s own motives. Jesus sent his disciples out with “freely ye have received, freely give”; Paul said “we preach not ourselves” and became “all things to all men”; the Prophet’s saying that deeds are judged by intentions is the Islamic statement of reading 11. Paul’s warning that eloquence without love is “sounding brass” stands beside reading 3.
questions: Why should the teacher’s motive matter to the hearer, if the words are true?
Reading 8 asks a teacher to learn a people’s literature and customs first. How is that an aspect of pure intention?
What are the ordinary impure motives in sharing one’s beliefs, and how would one know them in oneself?

outside.why: The teacher’s intention must be pure, his heart independent. We preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants.
A true servant to each member of humanity, by conduct and not words alone. Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister.
The thinkers of every age, for all their learning. Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
Teachers must not stain themselves with the world or look for the least reward. Freely ye have received, freely give. Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses.
The warning case in the New Testament: teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.
His resolution firm, his motive hidden. Let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.
That his essence of sincerity may be evident to all. Ye shall know them by their fruits.
The teacher of the Chinese people must be imbued with their spirit and know their sacred literature. Paul: I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.
Concentrate the soul on God, that it become a fountain for a thirsty world. He that believeth on me, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.
A pure soul will affect even stone. Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
First purge one’s heart and motives, or every enterprise is futile. The saying with which the great collections of hadith begin: the reward of deeds depends upon the intentions.
